Sparse optimization

Source: vignettes/sparse-optimization.Rmd
sparse-optimization.Rmd
library(optcompR)

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions, constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver Large models are built from vectors and sparse matrices, not from loops over scalars. Expressions store sparse triplets, and products with Matrix objects stay sparse all the way to the solver.

A sparse LP with 20 000 variables 

library(Matrix)
set.seed(1)
n <- 20000
k <- 2000
# every row gets at least one entry so the covering problem is feasible
A <- rsparsematrix(k, n, density = 5 / n, rand.x = function(m) runif(m, 0.5, 2)) +
  sparseMatrix(i = 1:k, j = sample(n, k), x = 1, dims = c(k, n))
b <- runif(k, 1, 10)
cost <- runif(n, 1, 3)

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = n, lower = 0)
build <- system.time({
  opt_constraint(m, A %*% x >= b, name = "cover")
  opt_objective(m, sum(cost * x))
})
build[["elapsed"]]
#> [1] 0.012
sf <- opt_standard_form(m)
dim(sf$A)
#> [1]  2000 20000
class(sf$A)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "Matrix"
r <- opt_solve(m)
opt_status(r)
#> [1] "optimal"
r$timing
#> build solve 
#> 0.002 0.059

One vector constraint gives k rows; there is one constraint block, so opt_dual(r, "cover") returns all k duals.

summary(opt_dual(r, "cover"))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.0000  0.2762  0.6998  0.6937  1.0110  2.9710

Sparse quadratic objectives

A least squares problem with a sparse design matrix and a ridge penalty:

p <- 500
X <- rsparsematrix(2000, p, density = 0.01)
beta <- rnorm(p)
y <- as.vector(X %*% beta) + rnorm(2000, sd = 0.1)
m2 <- opt_model()
bh <- opt_variable(m2, "beta", dim = p)
res <- X %*% bh - y
opt_objective(m2, sum(res^2) + 0.1 * sum(bh^2))
r2 <- opt_solve(m2)
opt_status(r2)
#> [1] "optimal"
sf2 <- opt_standard_form(m2)
c(nonzeros_in_Q = length(sf2$Q@x), size = nrow(sf2$Q))
#> nonzeros_in_Q          size 
#>         23153           500

Guidelines

  • Write A %*% x and sum(w * x) instead of loops when the data is a matrix.
  • Use one constraint block per family of rows; blocks keep names and duals organized and are much faster to build than many scalar constraints.
  • Parameters avoid rebuilding when only data changes (vignette("parameterized-models")).
